description: The two legacy Padova isochrone archives' characteristics and their mapping into the stellariso unified vocabulary (definitions in registry/unified_parameters.json). Loaded and validated together with the definitions by stellariso.registry.
notes: Sources are the two static CDS/VizieR catalogs, not the model team's site: padova/2000 = J/A+AS/141/371 (Girardi et al. 2000), padova/1994 = J/A+AS/106/275 (Bertelli et al. 1994); the original host pleiadi.pd.astro.it is effectively dead. Both catalogs publish no checksums; sha256 is computed at download and recorded.

Neither archive carries per-row evolutionary-stage columns. padova/2000 phases are anchored on the source's own isochsum.dat characteristic points (its G1 stage labels: TO, RGBb, RGBt, BHeb, EHeb, 1TP, AGBt, Cb); padova/1994 phases are derived by documented shape rules over the isochrone's own columns (the archive has no stage vocabulary at all). Both mappings are declared derived and versioned by mapping_version.

The files state neither composition nor release in their content: padova/1994 tables carry no header and no Z column, so each table's (Z, Y) comes from the catalog ReadMe's documented file list and the canonical file names table1..table6 are required; padova/2000 carries its Z and Overshoot as columns but its Y-per-Z pairing and the solar identification (Z=0.019) come from the ReadMe text.

[Fe/H] is a stellariso-declared conversion under the scaled-solar assumption: [Fe/H] = log10(Z/Z_ref) with each release's own solar Z (padova/2000: Z_ref = 0.019, ReadMe-declared solar composition; padova/1994: Z_ref = 0.02, the solar point of the paper's composition grid). The two references differ and are never shared across releases.

padova/2000 isochrones start at the ZAMS and end at the thermally pulsing AGB or carbon ignition (no post-AGB/WD rows); padova/1994 isochrones extend beyond the AGB tip to the white-dwarf stage after the planetary-nebula phase (paper abstract).

padova/2000 Mact can exceed Mini by up to ~5e-5 Msun on 1,177 of 64,381 rows — a print-precision artifact of Mact's F6.4 format against Mini's F10.8, not a physics violation; assertions must use the file's precision.

padova/1994 current mass M is non-monotonic within an isochrone by construction (ReadMe Note 1: it drops at the RGB-to-ZAHB and AGB-to-post-AGB transitions under the mass-loss prescription); initial_mass is recovered by inverting the tabulated FLUM and is non-decreasing in every published block.
padova/1994 star mass is M where Mwind = 0 and Mwind where Mwind > 0 (ReadMe Note 2: for massive stars the actual mass is the wind-reduced value; Mwind is printed only in the youngest isochrones).
The Reimers eta of both releases' RGB mass loss is stated in the papers, not in the catalog ReadMes; until extracted from the paper texts it is recorded implicit/not_reported rather than assumed.

references.citation: Girardi, L., Bressan, A., Bertelli, G., Chiosi, C. 2000, A&AS, 141, 371
Bertelli, G., Bressan, A., Chiosi, C., Fagotto, F., Nasi, E. 1994, A&AS, 106, 275

field_mappings.description: initial mass of the star whose evolution the row samples (Mini column)
actual mass including the mass-loss history (Mact column); can exceed Mini by up to ~5e-5 Msun through F6.4 print rounding

field_mappings.transformation: stage boundaries at the isochsum.dat characteristic-point initial masses of this isochrone (G1 labels): rows below M_TO are main_sequence; subgiant starts at M_TO; red_giant_branch at M_RGBb (or Brg); core_helium_burning at M_RGBt (or Tip, or BHeb); early_asymptotic_giant_branch at M_EHeb; thermally_pulsing_asymptotic_giant_branch at M_1TP. Interior markers (Te-m, Te-M, L-M, L-m) are not boundaries; a missing anchor extends the previous stage; rows beyond the last anchor keep it (massive isochrones end at C-ignition, Cb, and stay in the last AGB stage — the unified vocabulary has no carbon-ignition stage). Requires the isochsum.dat companion next to isochron.dat

field_mappings.description: no per-row phase column exists; the source's own stage labels appear only at isochsum.dat characteristic points and anchor the derived phase
no radius column is published; log_surface_gravity carries the size information the unified vocabulary needs
isochrones are tabulated in initial mass, not EEPs

parameters.name: log_age
parameters.description: log10(age/yr) as printed per row (F5.2); 7.80 to 10.25, step 0.05, in every (Overshoot, Z) column of the grid

parameters.name: initial_z
parameters.description: exact metallicity value of the isochrone (Z column); six published values 0.0004 to 0.03

parameters.name: initial_helium
parameters.description: one Y per published Z, from the ReadMe description ([0.0004,0.23], [0.001,0.23], [0.004,0.24], [0.008,0.25], [0.019,0.273] solar, [0.03,0.30]); not tabulated in the data file

parameters.name: overshoot
parameters.description: the Overshoot column: 1 = models with a moderate amount of convective overshoot (the whole grid), 0 = solar-comparison set computed with the classical Schwarzschild criterion (solar Z only)

parameters.name: initial_feh
parameters.description: scaled-solar conversion anchored on the ReadMe's declared solar composition [Z=0.019, Y=0.273]; a recorded parameter — the selection coordinate is the native initial_z

parameters.name: alpha_fe
parameters.description: the published composition sets are scaled-solar [Z, Y] pairs; the alpha-enhanced grids of the same generation are a separate publication (Salasnich et al. 2000)

parameters.name: initial_rotation
parameters.description: the models are non-rotating; no rotation axis exists in this release

parameters.name: eta_reimers
parameters.description: RGB mass loss with a Reimers-type law is in the models (Mact carries its history); the efficiency value is stated in the paper text, not in the catalog — record pending paper extraction

field_mappings.transformation: inversion of the tabulated Salpeter luminosity-function integral: FLUM = Mini^(1-alpha)/(1-alpha) with alpha = 2.35 and A = 1 (ReadMe note), so Mini = ((alpha-1) * |FLUM|)^(1/(1-alpha)); verified non-decreasing in every published block (the current-mass column is NOT, by construction)
M where Mwind = 0, Mwind where Mwind > 0 (ReadMe Note 2: for massive stars the actual mass is the wind-reduced value; Mwind is tabulated only in the youngest isochrones)

logL = (Mbol_sun - Mbol) / 2.5 with Mbol_sun = 4.77, the zero point of the same group's immediately following release (derivable exactly from Girardi et al. 2000's own paired logL and Mbol columns, spread 1e-3 = print rounding); the 1994 paper's stated constant has not been re-verified from the paper text

surface-gravity closure from the tabulated quantities: logg = log10(M/Msun) + 4 log10(Teff/Teff_sun) - log10(L/Lsun) + log10(g_sun) with g_sun = 10^4.438 cm/s2, Teff_sun = 5777 K, and L through the declared Mbol_sun = 4.77 chain; the constants are declared by this mapping, not stated by the source

field_mappings.native: shape rules over log(Teff), Mbol, M, FLUM
field_mappings.transformation: documented shape rules per isochrone (the archive publishes no stage vocabulary): main_sequence up to the turnoff, the first log(Teff) maximum followed by a >= 0.1 dex fall (the descent toward the giants; the global maximum would misfire on the youngest isochrones whose stripped Wolf-Rayet tail is hotter than any main-sequence star); red_giant_branch (subgiant not separated, the MIST phase-2 precedent) up to the first logL local maximum followed by a >= 0.15 dex decrease (the RGB tip; the RGB-to-HB mass drop that follows completes it); core_helium_burning until logL re-exceeds that tip luminosity; early_asymptotic_giant_branch until the second current-mass drop (AGB-to-post-AGB, told from the RGB drop by the post-drop luminosity staying within 0.3 dex of the tip); post_agb up to the tail's maximum log(Teff); white_dwarf after it; and wolf_rayet for post-turnoff rows hotter than the turnoff with initial mass above 10 Msun (stripped massive cores — the unified vocabulary's stage for them; nothing else in these isochrones can be both). A block whose chain does not resolve consistently is classified 'unknown' with a warning, never guessed

field_mappings.description: the archive publishes no stage vocabulary at all; the derived phase is pure shape analysis of the source's own columns
no radius column is published; log_surface_gravity carries the size information the unified vocabulary needs
isochrones are tabulated in luminosity-function order, not EEPs

parameters.name: log_age
parameters.description: log10(age/yr) as printed per row (F6.3); 6.60 to 10.30 across the six tables (one table carries 6.60 to 10.24)

parameters.name: initial_z
parameters.description: per-table Z from the catalog ReadMe's file list (the data files state no composition): table1 0.0004, table2 0.001, table3 0.004, table4 0.008, table5 0.02, table6 0.05 — the canonical file names are therefore required

parameters.name: initial_helium
parameters.description: per-table Y from the same ReadMe list: 0.23, 0.23, 0.24, 0.25, 0.28, 0.352; the table2 set is computed with Huebner et al. (1977) opacities, the rest with Iglesias et al. (1992)

parameters.name: initial_feh
parameters.description: scaled-solar conversion anchored on the paper grid's solar composition [Z=0.02, Y=0.28] (the Padova-1994 generation's solar point); differs from padova/2000's 0.019 — each release declares its own; a recorded parameter — the selection coordinate is the native initial_z

parameters.name: alpha_fe
parameters.description: the published composition sets are scaled-solar [Z, Y] pairs

parameters.name: initial_rotation
parameters.description: the models are non-rotating; no rotation axis exists in this release

parameters.name: overshoot
parameters.description: the convective-overshoot setting of the 1994 isochrone models is described in the paper text, not in the catalog ReadMe

parameters.name: eta_reimers
parameters.description: mass loss enters the tabulated current mass (ReadMe Note 1 describes the RGB and TP-AGB prescriptions by paper section); the efficiency values are stated in the paper text, not in the catalog — record pending paper extraction
